description: Frontier model kept brief: rarely appropriate, mainly for quick top-tier judgment calls on ambiguous work without a long session.
Frontier model at normal reasoning depth: strong default when a task needs top-tier judgment but isn't yet a multi-day effort.
Ambitious, codebase-spanning features, deep code review, or performance work needing sustained, careful reasoning across many files.
The hardest, longest-horizon work: multi-day autonomous sessions, root-cause fixes on ambiguous architecture problems, avoiding shortcuts.
Strongest model kept brief: quick opinions or small edits where top-tier judgment matters more than exhaustive reasoning.
Strong general-purpose coding with normal reasoning depth, for moderately complex features or bugs.
Complex multi-file implementation, tricky debugging, or non-obvious design tradeoffs.
Hardest tasks: system/architecture redesign, subtle concurrency or distributed bugs, deep unfamiliar-codebase investigation.
Trivial edits: renames, formatting, single-file mechanical changes.
Default for normal feature work and isolated bug fixes with typical reasoning needs.
Multi-file refactors or debugging that needs careful reasoning but not the largest model.
Demanding reasoning tasks where a fast/strong balance is preferred over the largest model.
Fastest, cheapest option for trivial, mechanical, low-risk changes.
Simple, well-specified tasks that need a bit more care than the lowest tier.
Rarely appropriate; a smaller model reasoning hard, useful mainly for cost-constrained but non-trivial tasks.
Edge case: exhaust the smallest model's reasoning before escalating to a larger one.
